memory_candidates.content: Proving a cut/substitution-admissibility lemma over a List-indexed natural-deduction judgment (context growth via impI/orE/diaE-style rules that prepend to the front) cannot be done via `induction h generalizing Delta` directly when the scrutinee's context index is a compound term like `Delta ++ (y:B)::Gamma` (not a plain variable) -- Lean's induction tactic handles indexed families cleanly only when the index is itself a bare local variable. The fix: state a separate auxiliary lemma that is fully generalized over an explicit list variable Gamma0 PLUS an equation hypothesis `Gamma0 = Delta' ++ (y:B)::Gamma` and the substituting-derivation hypothesis, both kept INSIDE the not-yet-introduced goal (as a `forall`) before running `induction`, so the induction's motive naturally varies Delta' (and, if the judgment also indexes on a graph/environment that changes in some constructors, that too) per branch. Growing-context constructors then invoke the IH at `Delta'' := (item :: Delta')`, closed by `rw [heq, List.cons_append]` (plain `rw [heq]` alone does not auto-close list-append/cons associativity via its automatic rfl attempt).

reflection.what_worked: Reading the prior dispatch's docstring (which already diagnosed the exact induction shape needed: generalize over an accumulating prefix Delta, re-weaken at each level) meant the design was settled before the first tool call -- no exploration needed, straight to writing the auxiliary lemma. Mirroring NIK.weaken's exact case order and structure (already sorry-free in the same file) made each of the 13 NIK constructors mechanical to handle.
reflection.what_was_hard: Two subtleties needed real reasoning, not just pattern-matching: (1) recognizing that induction on a compound context index (Delta++(y:B)::Gamma) required a separate fully-generalized auxiliary lemma rather than `induction h generalizing Delta` directly, and (2) that the boxI/diaE branches needed hsub re-weakened to the branch's extended graph (G.addEdge x w), not threaded as a single fixed hypothesis, since those two constructors' recursive premises genuinely live at a different graph.
reflection.what_was_missed: Underestimated on the first pass that `rw [heq]`'s automatic post-rewrite rfl would not close the cons/append associativity goals on its own; needed an explicit `List.cons_append` rewrite added after the first build attempt surfaced the four unsolved goals.
reflection.successes: NIK.subst closed sorry-free on essentially the first structurally-correct attempt (one build iteration to fix the cons_append goals). TPrime clause 1 (deductive closure) and deductiveClosure_of_maximal are now unconditionally sorry-free, confirmed via lean_verify. Sorry count in the probe dropped from 3 to 2. Zero Cslib/ mainline files touched; zero-debt invariant held.
